polars:position-deletes:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): not supported as a write operation. pl.delete_iceberg on a table that requests write.delete.mode=merge-on-read wrote no position delete file: PyIceberg warned "Merge on read is not yet supported, falling back to copy-on-write" and rewrote the data file. Polars does read position delete files written by other engines (a Spark-written one was applied natively), but that is a read capability, not this operation.
caveats: Read capability only: the native reader applies position delete files written by other engines
pl.delete_iceberg always rewrites data files (copy-on-write) through PyIceberg

polars:position-deletes:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg on a Spark-created V3 table that requests merge-on-read is refused with "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3", so Polars writes neither position delete files nor the deletion vectors that replace them in V3. The native reader does apply a Spark-written deletion vector (Puffin), but that is a read capability.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"
Read capability only: a Spark-written Puffin deletion vector is applied by the native, PyIceberg and automatic readers

polars:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): not supported as a write operation: pl.delete_iceberg wrote no equality delete file. Polars also cannot read a table that contains one: scanning a table with a Java-API equality delete raised "PyIceberg does not yet support equality deletes" (with the native reader and with reader_override='pyiceberg').
caveats: Reading a table that contains equality deletes fails (the PyIceberg fallback refuses it)

links.label: Iceberg: equality delete support in PyIceberg (apache/iceberg#6568)

polars:equality-deletes:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg on a V3 table is refused, so no delete file of any kind can be written. A V3 table that contains a Java-API equality delete cannot be read either: "PyIceberg does not yet support equality deletes" (same as V2).
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"
Reading a V3 table that contains equality deletes fails (the PyIceberg fallback refuses it)

links.label: Iceberg: equality delete support in PyIceberg (apache/iceberg#6568)

polars:merge-on-read:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): not supported as a write operation. With write.delete.mode=merge-on-read set on the table, pl.delete_iceberg still produced no delete file: PyIceberg warned that merge-on-read is not supported and fell back to copy-on-write.
caveats: Polars can read merge-on-read tables written by other engines (position deletes, V3 deletion vectors), but not produce them

polars:merge-on-read:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg on a V3 table fails, so no merge-on-read write is possible.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:copy-on-write:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg(table, predicate) rewrote the affected data file (snapshot operation overwrite, no delete files) and the deleted row disappeared. Copy-on-write is the only delete strategy Polars has; write_iceberg(mode='overwrite') and sink_iceberg(mode='overwrite') also rewrite. Also measured on a table partitioned by day(ts) and bucket(4, name): pl.delete_iceberg rewrote one file inside a partition (snapshot operation overwrite, data files only) and write_iceberg(mode='overwrite') replaced the table contents.
caveats: Delegates to PyIceberg's copy-on-write delete; rewrites whole data files, not row ranges

polars:copy-on-write:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg on a V3 table fails, so copy-on-write cannot be used on V3 tables.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:schema-evolution:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN and DROP COLUMN apply to the table, and a renamed column keeps its field id. sink_iceberg(schema_mode='merge' / 'overwrite') also evolves the schema as part of a write.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)
Polars 1.44 release post (Iceberg sink schema evolution, v3 deletion vectors on scan)

polars:schema-evolution:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER TABLE ADD, RENAME and DROP COLUMN apply to a Spark-written V3 table (metadata-only commits; rows still read). Evolving the schema as part of a data write is still refused on V3.
caveats: Data writes to V3 tables are refused, so new columns can only be filled by another engine

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:type-promotion:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): appending Int64, Float64 and Decimal(18,2) data with sink_iceberg(schema_mode='merge') to a table with int, float and decimal(9,2) columns promoted them to long, double and decimal(18,2), and the existing row still read correctly. Without schema_mode the wider frame is refused. The other direction was measured too: appending Int32, Float32 and Decimal(9,2) data to the now-wide columns is refused without schema_mode (a to_arrow() conversion error: Polars does not cast to the table type), and with schema_mode='merge' it is accepted while the table keeps long, double and decimal(18,2); a column is never narrowed.
caveats: Promotion is implicit on write; there is no standalone widening operation
Only widening is performed. Narrower data never changes the table: it is refused without schema_mode and appended into the wide column type with schema_mode='merge'
schema_mode is marked unstable in the Polars docs

polars:type-promotion:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE promotes int to long, float to double and decimal(9,2) to decimal(18,2) on a Spark-written V3 table, and the existing row still reads. Promoting through a data write (sink_iceberg schema_mode='merge') is refused on V3.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:column-default-values:v2.notes: Column default values is a V3 feature, not applicable to format version 2

polars:column-default-values:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): the native and automatic readers apply the V3 initial-default on read: a row written before the column existed returns the default ('eu'). Write defaults cannot be applied: appending a row without the column to the V3 table is refused with "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3".
caveats: Read-side only: initial-default honoured; write-default needs V3 writes
V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:table-creation:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL CREATE TABLE ... WITH (properties) on a catalog attached through SQLContext.register_catalog creates a table with the requested format version and properties, ALTER TABLE ... SET PARTITIONED BY adds a partition spec, and INSERT writes to it. sink_iceberg(create_if_not_exists=True) still creates unpartitioned V2 tables from a frame.
caveats: Partitioning is a second statement: CREATE TABLE ... PARTITIONED BY does not parse
The SQL catalog API is marked unstable

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:table-creation:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL CREATE TABLE ... WITH ('format-version'='3') creates an empty V3 table, but Polars cannot partition it (SET PARTITIONED BY on a V3 table is not supported yet) or write rows into it.
caveats: CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT with format-version 3 is refused

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER TABLE ... SET PARTITIONED BY declares day(ts) + bucket(4, name) on a table it created, and its INSERT writes one file per partition. write_iceberg and sink_iceberg write correct partition values, and predicates prune files for identity, bucket, truncate, year, month, day and hour transforms.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:hidden-partitioning:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): on a V3 table partitioned by day(ts) and bucket(4, name), written with Spark because Polars' own write_iceberg and sink_iceberg appends are refused, a ts predicate planned only the matching files and returned the right rows. Spark-written V3 tables partitioned by identity(id), truncate(2, name), year(ts), month(ts) and hour(ts) were pruned the same way (1 of 3 or 4 files planned).
caveats: Read-side only; V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:partition-evolution:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER TABLE ... SET PARTITIONED BY evolves a partitioned table's spec in place (kept fields keep their names); sink_iceberg then writes under the new spec and scan_iceberg reads across both.
caveats: SET PARTITIONED BY is refused on V3 tables

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:partition-evolution:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): scan_iceberg read a V3 table across an evolved partition spec (the spec was evolved with PyIceberg and the data written with Spark). Polars' own sink_iceberg append under the new spec is refused on V3.
caveats: Read-side only; cannot evolve a spec, and V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:multi-arg-transforms:v2.notes: Multi-argument transforms is a V3 feature, not applicable to format version 2

polars:multi-arg-transforms:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars' Iceberg layer is PyIceberg's metadata model, which drops source-ids from a partition field (it does not model multi-argument transforms), and no Polars write function takes a partition spec. Spark with Iceberg 1.11 refuses to create such a table ("Cannot convert transform with more than one column reference: bucket(4, a, b)"), so there is no table to read.
caveats: Not yet implemented in PyIceberg

polars:time-travel:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL FOR VERSION AS OF <snapshot id> and FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF <timestamp> return historical rows (a timestamp between two commits returned the earlier state). scan_iceberg(snapshot_id=...) and incremental append scans also work.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:time-travel:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): On a Spark-written V3 table, Polars SQL FOR VERSION AS OF and FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF return the historical rows, as does scan_iceberg(snapshot_id=...).

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:table-maintenance:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL CALL lake.system.rewrite_data_files compacted three small data files into one (rows intact), and rewrite_manifests runs. There is no snapshot expiry or orphan-file removal: CALL supports only add_files, rewrite_data_files and rewrite_manifests.
caveats: Compaction needs options => map('rewrite-all','true') for tables under the default size thresholds

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:table-maintenance:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL CALL rewrite_data_files is refused on a V3 table (not supported yet), and there is no other maintenance operation.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:branching-tagging:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL ALTER TABLE ... CREATE/DROP BRANCH and CREATE/DROP TAG manage refs, and FOR VERSION AS OF '<ref>' reads a branch or tag. No Polars write targets a branch: INSERT INTO <table>.branch_<name> is not recognised, so writes always go to main.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:branching-tagging:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): On a Spark-written V3 table Polars SQL creates and drops tags and branches and reads them with FOR VERSION AS OF '<ref>'. Writes to V3 tables are refused, and no Polars write targets a branch.

links.label: Polars SQL writes to attached Iceberg catalogs (pola-rs/polars#30463)

polars:read-support:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.scan_iceberg() read a Spark-created V2 table through the REST catalog, with projection and predicate pushdown into the scan. Position delete files are applied natively; the query is planned by the native polars-iceberg reader and falls back to PyIceberg for table features it does not handle. A table that contains an equality delete (attached with the Iceberg Java API, as a Flink upsert sink would) cannot be loaded at all: the native, PyIceberg and automatic readers all raised ValueError "PyIceberg does not yet support equality deletes: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/6568". Rated partial because tables written by upsert pipelines fail to load.
caveats: Tables that contain equality delete files cannot be loaded, whichever reader is used (ValueError: PyIceberg does not yet support equality deletes: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/6568)
scan_iceberg is marked unstable in the Polars docs

links.label: Iceberg: equality delete support in PyIceberg (apache/iceberg#6568)

polars:read-support:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): the native reader read a Spark-created V3 table that carries a deletion vector (V3 deletion vectors are read natively since Polars 1.44). Initial column defaults, unknown-type and nanosecond-timestamp columns also read correctly. As in V2, a V3 table that contains an equality delete cannot be loaded (ValueError "PyIceberg does not yet support equality deletes: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/6568").
caveats: Tables that contain equality delete files cannot be loaded, whichever reader is used
V3 tables with a variant or geometry column cannot be read (see Variant Type and Geometry / Geo Types)

links.label: Polars 1.44 release post (Iceberg sink schema evolution, v3 deletion vectors on scan)

polars:write-insert:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): DataFrame.write_iceberg(mode='append') and LazyFrame.sink_iceberg(mode='append') both appended to a table through the REST catalog, and sink_iceberg(mode='overwrite') replaced the contents.
caveats: write_iceberg goes through PyIceberg; sink_iceberg writes Parquet natively and commits through PyIceberg
sink_iceberg needs explicit S3 storage_options: it does not take them from the catalog or table

polars:write-insert:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): appending to a V3 table with write_iceberg or sink_iceberg fails.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:write-merge-update-delete:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars SQL UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE INTO (matched update and not-matched insert) apply to catalog tables and leave the right rows. All three are copy-on-write. The DataFrame API still offers only pl.delete_iceberg and sink_iceberg(overwrite_filter=...).
caveats: The SQL catalog API is marked unstable

polars:write-merge-update-delete:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): pl.delete_iceberg on a V3 table fails.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:catalog-integration:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): Polars read and wrote through two PyIceberg catalog types: the Iceberg REST catalog and a SQL (SQLite) catalog. The catalog= argument accepts any PyIceberg catalog or a polars IcebergCatalogConfig, so Polars has no catalog client of its own.
caveats: Catalog support is whatever PyIceberg provides
Only the REST catalog (Apache Polaris) and a SQL catalog (SQLite) were exercised. Glue, Hive, DynamoDB and the other PyIceberg catalog types were not tested, and the Glue test only reports skip

polars:catalog-integration:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): a V3 table was loaded and read through the REST catalog; writing to it is refused.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:statistics:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): files written by sink_iceberg carry column lower/upper bounds in the manifest, and a predicate scan planned only the files whose bounds can match (1 of 2). The manifest also holds per-column null and value counts (a column with one null in four rows reported 1 and 4). With the table's data files deleted, scan_iceberg(use_metadata_statistics=True) still answered a row count of 3, so the native reader does answer row counts from metadata alone.
caveats: use_metadata_statistics and fast_deletion_count are marked unstable in the Polars docs

polars:statistics:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): on Spark-written V3 files a predicate scan planned only the matching file.
caveats: Read-side only; V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:bloom-filters:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): neither sink_iceberg nor write_iceberg produced a Parquet bloom filter for a column with write.parquet.bloom-filter-enabled.column.id=true, and Puffin bloom blobs are not used.
caveats: The table property is ignored

polars:bloom-filters:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): no write path works on a V3 table, and the property is ignored on V2.
caveats: V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"

polars:rest-catalog:v2.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): full round-trip through the Iceberg REST catalog (Apache Polaris, OAuth2 client credentials, S3 storage): create with sink_iceberg, append with write_iceberg, read with scan_iceberg, drop through PyIceberg.
caveats: The catalog connection is a PyIceberg RestCatalog

polars:variant-type:v2.notes: Variant type is a V3 feature, not applicable to format version 2

Error raised: TypeError "ValidationError.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'line_errors'" while PyIceberg parses the table schema

A table written by Spark with write.parquet.shred-variants=true (typed_value columns confirmed in the Parquet file) cannot be loaded either: the same schema-parsing error as for an unshredded variant column.

polars:geometry-type:v2.notes: Geometry type is a V3 feature, not applicable to format version 2

polars:geometry-type:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): a DuckDB-written V3 table with a GEOMETRY column cannot be read: the native reader fails on the Parquet GEOMETRY logical type ("LogicalType union has no variant set") and the PyIceberg reader fails with "Cannot promote an binary to geometry". An empty V3 table with a GEOGRAPHY column (made with the Iceberg Java API) loads and the column maps to Binary; no engine in the test setup can write a GEOGRAPHY value, so GEOGRAPHY data was not tested. Polars has no geometry dtype and cannot write to V3 tables.
caveats: Both readers fail on the table
GEOGRAPHY: only an empty table could be tested (loads as Binary); no GEOGRAPHY data was read

polars:nanosecond-timestamps:v2.notes: Nanosecond timestamps is a V3 feature, not applicable to format version 2

polars:nanosecond-timestamps:v3.notes: Measured (Polars 2.2.0, PyIceberg 0.12.0): a DuckDB-written V3 timestamp_ns table reads as Datetime('ns') with the sub-microsecond digits intact (123456789). Polars cannot write nanosecond timestamps: write_iceberg raises "Nanosecond resolution temporal type ... is not safely convertible to microseconds", sink_iceberg raises UnsupportedPyArrowTypeException ("unsupported type: timestamp[ns]"), and creating a table from a nanosecond frame raises "columns without a lossless Iceberg type".
caveats: Read-side only; V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"
Writing a Datetime("ns") frame fails in every write path, even before the V3 write refusal is reached

caveats: Read capability: V3 row-lineage metadata is parsed, lineage columns are not exposed

It can read them: the native, PyIceberg and automatic readers applied a Spark-written Puffin deletion vector (added in Polars 1.44), but that is a read capability, not this operation.

V3 write is not supported: every Polars write path (write_iceberg, sink_iceberg, delete_iceberg) fails on a V3 table with PyIceberg's "Cannot write manifest for table version: 3"
